frases.texto: Don Quixote of La Mancha. Part 2: Woolly Armies and the Magic Helmet
frases.fala: Don Quixote of La Mancha. Part 2: Woolly Armies and the Magic Helmet

frases.texto: Lance in hand and brave of heart, Don Quixote gallops against the windmill giants, and his loyal squire Sancho Panza follows close behind, along the sunny roads of La Mancha!
frases.fala: Lance in hand and brave of heart, Don Quixote gallops against the windmill giants, and his loyal squire Sancho Panza follows close behind, along the sunny roads of La Mancha!

frases.texto: In this part of the story, our knight will take a spectacular tumble, get a new lance under the stars, have supper with some GOATHERDS, fight armies in the middle of the dust, get a nickname nobody forgets and win a HELMET that shines like the sun.
frases.fala: In this part of the story, our knight will take a spectacular tumble, get a new lance under the stars, have supper with some goatherds, fight armies in the middle of the dust, get a nickname nobody forgets and win a helmet that shines like the sun.

frases.texto: Open your eyes and your heart wide, and get your IMAGINATION ready: the biggest adventures are only just beginning!
frases.fala: Open your eyes and your heart wide, and get your imagination ready: the biggest adventures are only just beginning!

frases.texto: Chapter 8. The Attack on the Giants. The Flight and the Fall at the Windmills!
frases.fala: Chapter 8. The Attack on the Giants. The Flight and the Fall at the Windmills!

frases.texto: With the brass basin on his head and his lance held tight, Don Quixote made gentle Rocinante set off at a brave gallop.
frases.fala: With the brass basin on his head and his lance held tight, Don Quixote made gentle Rocinante set off at a brave gallop.

frases.texto: “Don’t run away, you cowardly giants!
frases.fala: Don’t run away, you cowardly giants!

frases.texto: Only one knight is coming to fight you all!” he shouted, charging at the first WINDMILL in the field!
frases.fala: Only one knight is coming to fight you all! he shouted, charging at the first windmill in the field!

frases.texto: Just then, a strong wind blew, and the huge wooden sail spun round fast and broke the tip of his LANCE into a thousand little pieces!
frases.fala: Just then, a strong wind blew, and the huge wooden sail spun round fast and broke the tip of his lance into a thousand little pieces!

frases.texto: With one spectacular tug, the sail lifted horse and rider high up, whirled them round the sky and dropped them both, with a great big bump, on the soft grass!
frases.fala: With one spectacular tug, the sail lifted horse and rider high up, whirled them round the sky and dropped them both, with a great big bump, on the soft grass!

frases.texto: Sancho came rushing up on his donkey, holding his head in a fright: “Oh my goodness, my lord!
frases.fala: Sancho came rushing up on his donkey, holding his head in a fright: Oh my goodness, my lord!

frases.texto: Didn’t I tell you they were only windmills?”
frases.fala: Didn’t I tell you they were only windmills?

frases.texto: But Don Quixote shook off the dust, straightened his dented basin and explained, very calmly: “Hush, friend Sancho!
frases.fala: But Don Quixote shook off the dust, straightened his dented basin and explained, very calmly: Hush, friend Sancho!

frases.texto: In a knight’s adventures, everything changes in the blink of an eye!
frases.fala: In a knight’s adventures, everything changes in the blink of an eye!

frases.texto: It was the wicked wizard Frestón who cast a SPELL and turned the giants into windmills, just to steal my victory.
frases.fala: It was the wicked wizard Frestón who cast a spell and turned the giants into windmills, just to steal my victory.

frases.texto: But no magic can beat our COURAGE!”
frases.fala: But no magic can beat our courage!

frases.texto: Chapter 9. The Oak Lance. A New Lance under the Stars
frases.fala: Chapter 9. The Oak Lance. A New Lance under the Stars

frases.texto: Even though his body ached from the fall and his brass basin was all dented, Don Quixote did not give up.
frases.fala: Even though his body ached from the fall and his brass basin was all dented, Don Quixote did not give up.

frases.texto: “A true knight never gives in to sadness!” he said, patting his loyal Rocinante.
frases.fala: A true knight never gives in to sadness! he said, patting his loyal Rocinante.

frases.texto: He walked over to an old, leafy OAK TREE by the side of the road, chose a dry branch, straight and strong, and proudly made it into his brand-new LANCE.
frases.fala: He walked over to an old, leafy oak tree by the side of the road, chose a dry branch, straight and strong, and proudly made it into his brand-new lance.

frases.texto: “A hero of Spain long ago lost his sword in a battle, so he fought with a tree trunk and won!” he told Sancho.
frases.fala: A hero of Spain long ago lost his sword in a battle, so he fought with a tree trunk and won! he told Sancho.

frases.texto: “And I shall do just the same!”
frases.fala: And I shall do just the same!

frases.texto: When night came, soft and cool, Sancho spread straw on the ground, ate his little bit of cheese and fell into such a deep sleep that his snores sounded like bells ringing on the hill.
frases.fala: When night came, soft and cool, Sancho spread straw on the ground, ate his little bit of cheese and fell into such a deep sleep that his snores sounded like bells ringing on the hill.

frases.texto: But Don Quixote stayed awake, watching the twinkling STARS and thinking of his sweet DULCINEA, just like the knights in his books.
frases.fala: But Don Quixote stayed awake, watching the twinkling stars and thinking of his sweet dulcinea, just like the knights in his books.

frases.texto: Chapter 10. The Goatherds and the Golden Age. A Supper to Share
frases.fala: Chapter 10. The Goatherds and the Golden Age. A Supper to Share

frases.texto: Late the next afternoon, smelling the lovely smell of a campfire, the two friends found six GOATHERDS sitting together in the field.
frases.fala: Late the next afternoon, smelling the lovely smell of a campfire, the two friends found six goatherds sitting together in the field.

frases.texto: They didn’t ask any questions or stare at the rusty armour.
frases.fala: They didn’t ask any questions or stare at the rusty armour.

frases.texto: They just smiled and spread a soft sheepskin on the ground.
frases.fala: They just smiled and spread a soft sheepskin on the ground.

frases.texto: “Sit down, friends!” said the oldest goatherd.
frases.fala: Sit down, friends! said the oldest goatherd.

frases.texto: “Here, what belongs to one belongs to all!”
frases.fala: Here, what belongs to one belongs to all!

frases.texto: Happily, they shared the best things they had: a bowl of ACORNS, the little nuts of the oak tree, roasted on the fire, a big piece of goat’s CHEESE and a jug of fresh MILK.
frases.fala: Happily, they shared the best things they had: a bowl of acorns, the little nuts of the oak tree, roasted on the fire, a big piece of goat’s cheese and a jug of fresh milk.

frases.texto: Help lay the goatherds’ table!
frases.fala: Help lay the goatherds’ table!

frases.texto: Holding the acorns in his hand, Don Quixote spoke with great feeling: “Once there was a very happy time, the GOLDEN AGE, when nobody built fences and everybody knew how to SHARE the fruits of the earth with love!”
frases.fala: Holding the acorns in his hand, Don Quixote spoke with great feeling: Once there was a very happy time, the golden age, when nobody built fences and everybody knew how to share the fruits of the earth with love!

frases.texto: The goatherds didn’t understand all of the knight’s difficult words, but they felt the warmth of his kind heart.
frases.fala: The goatherds didn’t understand all of the knight’s difficult words, but they felt the warmth of his kind heart.

frases.texto: After all, the world becomes a magic place whenever we know how to share!
frases.fala: After all, the world becomes a magic place whenever we know how to share!

frases.texto: Chapter 11. The Armies of Dust. The Great Battle of the Sheep
frases.fala: Chapter 11. The Armies of Dust. The Great Battle of the Sheep

frases.texto: One sunny morning, riding across the endless fields of La Mancha, Don Quixote suddenly stopped and pointed his lance at the horizon.
frases.fala: One sunny morning, riding across the endless fields of La Mancha, Don Quixote suddenly stopped and pointed his lance at the horizon.

frases.texto: Two enormous clouds of DUST were rushing towards each other, covering the sky like an earth-coloured blanket!
frases.fala: Two enormous clouds of dust were rushing towards each other, covering the sky like an earth-coloured blanket!

frases.texto: “Be brave, faithful Sancho!” cried the knight, full of joy.
frases.fala: Be brave, faithful Sancho! cried the knight, full of joy.

frases.texto: “Here come two gigantic ARMIES!
frases.fala: Here come two gigantic armies!

frases.texto: On the left comes the terrible Alifanfarón of Trapobana; on the right, brave Pentapolín of the Rolled-Up Sleeve, who always fights with his sleeves rolled up!”
frases.fala: On the left comes the terrible Alifanfarón of Trapobana; on the right, brave Pentapolín of the Rolled-Up Sleeve, who always fights with his sleeves rolled up!

frases.texto: “But, my lord...” said Sancho, listening hard and frowning, “I can’t hear any swords or trumpets, just lots of baaaa!”
frases.fala: But, my lord... said Sancho, listening hard and frowning, I can’t hear any swords or trumpets, just lots of baaaa!

frases.texto: Blow away the dust and see the truth with your own eyes!
frases.fala: Blow away the dust and see the truth with your own eyes!

frases.texto: They were only two flocks of SHEEP eating grass!
frases.fala: They were only two flocks of sheep eating grass!

frases.texto: But Don Quixote was already galloping down the hill.
frases.fala: But Don Quixote was already galloping down the hill.

frases.texto: Frightened by that strange knight, the shepherds threw little stones with their slings to protect their animals.
frases.fala: Frightened by that strange knight, the shepherds threw little stones with their slings to protect their animals.

frases.texto: The poor knight fell off his horse in the middle of the field, with a sore chin and two teeth missing from his smile!
frases.fala: The poor knight fell off his horse in the middle of the field, with a sore chin and two teeth missing from his smile!

frases.texto: Chapter 12. The Knight of the Sorrowful Face. A Nickname Nobody Forgets
frases.fala: Chapter 12. The Knight of the Sorrowful Face. A Nickname Nobody Forgets

frases.texto: When night covered the fields in shadow, the two friends stopped to rest by a quiet road.
frases.fala: When night covered the fields in shadow, the two friends stopped to rest by a quiet road.

frases.texto: Seeing his master so quiet and sad, Sancho held up a little tin LANTERN to look at the knight’s bumps and bruises.
frases.fala: Seeing his master so quiet and sad, Sancho held up a little tin lantern to look at the knight’s bumps and bruises.

frases.texto: In the yellow candlelight, there was a face that made you feel sorry for him: Don Quixote was thin and tired from the battle, with his dented basin sitting crooked on his head and a funny little window in his smile, right where two teeth used to be.
frases.fala: In the yellow candlelight, there was a face that made you feel sorry for him: Don Quixote was thin and tired from the battle, with his dented basin sitting crooked on his head and a funny little window in his smile, right where two teeth used to be.

frases.texto: “My lord,” said Sancho kindly, with a cheeky smile, “you have the saddest, sorriest face I have ever seen in my life!
frases.fala: My lord, said Sancho kindly, with a cheeky smile, you have the saddest, sorriest face I have ever seen in my life!

frases.texto: I think your hero’s name should be the Knight of the SORROWFUL FACE!”
frases.fala: I think your hero’s name should be the Knight of the sorrowful face!

frases.texto: Instead of getting cross, Don Quixote loved the nickname!
frases.fala: Instead of getting cross, Don Quixote loved the nickname!

frases.texto: “What a beautiful name, Sancho!” he cried.
frases.fala: What a beautiful name, Sancho! he cried.

frases.texto: “All the great knights in books have names like poems.
frases.fala: All the great knights in books have names like poems.

frases.texto: I shall have a noble, thoughtful face painted on my SHIELD!”
frases.fala: I shall have a noble, thoughtful face painted on my shield!

frases.texto: Chapter 13. Noises in the Dark. The Goats that Cross the River
frases.fala: Chapter 13. Noises in the Dark. The Goats that Cross the River

frases.texto: On a night as black as coal, the two friends stopped near a wood of tall trees.
frases.fala: On a night as black as coal, the two friends stopped near a wood of tall trees.

frases.texto: Suddenly, a loud, scary noise began to echo through the leaves: THUMP-THUMP!
frases.fala: Suddenly, a loud, scary noise began to echo through the leaves: thump, thump!

frases.texto: THUMP-THUMP!
frases.fala: thump, thump!

frases.texto: It sounded like a giant hammering iron in the middle of the forest.
frases.fala: It sounded like a giant hammering iron in the middle of the forest.

frases.texto: Don Quixote grabbed his lance at once: “Who’s there?
frases.fala: Don Quixote grabbed his lance at once: Who’s there?

frases.texto: Come out, giant of the dark!”
frases.fala: Come out, giant of the dark!

frases.texto: Sancho, shaking like a jelly, had a very clever idea: he secretly tied Rocinante’s legs together, so the horse couldn’t take a single step.
frases.fala: Sancho, shaking like a jelly, had a very clever idea: he secretly tied Rocinante’s legs together, so the horse couldn’t take a single step.

frases.texto: And, to keep his master there until the sun came up, he began to tell a story that never ended:
frases.fala: And, to keep his master there until the sun came up, he began to tell a story that never ended:

frases.texto: “Once upon a time there was a shepherd called Lope Ruiz, who had to take three hundred GOATS to the other side of a very deep river.
frases.fala: Once upon a time there was a shepherd called Lope Ruiz, who had to take three hundred goats to the other side of a very deep river.

frases.texto: But he only had a teeny-tiny BOAT, with room for just one goat at a time!
frases.fala: But he only had a teeny-tiny boat, with room for just one goat at a time!

frases.texto: Now, listen carefully and don’t forget to COUNT every little goat that crosses... because if you lose count, the story stops right there!”
frases.fala: Now, listen carefully and don’t forget to count every little goat that crosses... because if you lose count, the story stops right there!

frases.texto: Help Don Quixote count the goats crossing the river!
frases.fala: Help Don Quixote count the goats crossing the river!

frases.texto: Chapter 14. The Secret of the Dawn. Who Went THUMP-THUMP?
frases.fala: Chapter 14. The Secret of the Dawn. Who Went thump, thump?

frases.texto: The night seemed to go on for ever.
frases.fala: The night seemed to go on for ever.

frases.texto: But, little by little, the sky turned gold and pink as the SUNRISE came.
frases.fala: But, little by little, the sky turned gold and pink as the sunrise came.

frases.texto: Tap the sun to wake up the day and chase the shadows away!
frases.fala: Tap the sun to wake up the day and chase the shadows away!

frases.texto: In the morning light, the friends at last found out the mystery of the night: no monsters, no beasts with sharp claws!
frases.fala: In the morning light, the friends at last found out the mystery of the night: no monsters, no beasts with sharp claws!

frases.texto: They were only six huge wooden HAMMERS, which the river water made beat, again and again, on pieces of cloth, to make them soft and fluffy.
frases.fala: They were only six huge wooden hammers, which the river water made beat, again and again, on pieces of cloth, to make them soft and fluffy.

frases.texto: THUMP-THUMP!
frases.fala: thump, thump!

frases.texto: THUMP-THUMP!
frases.fala: thump, thump!

frases.texto: When he saw that he had been scared for nothing, Sancho couldn’t help it: he held his tummy and let out such a big LAUGH that it echoed across the hills, and he nearly fell off his donkey: “Oh, my lord!
frases.fala: When he saw that he had been scared for nothing, Sancho couldn’t help it: he held his tummy and let out such a big laugh that it echoed across the hills, and he nearly fell off his donkey: Oh, my lord!

frases.texto: The giant of the night was a hammer for beating cloth!”
frases.fala: The giant of the night was a hammer for beating cloth!

frases.texto: Don Quixote looked serious at first, but soon he started laughing too.
frases.fala: Don Quixote looked serious at first, but soon he started laughing too.

frases.texto: After all, even the greatest heroes are afraid of what they don’t know, and the morning light always brings the truth!
frases.fala: After all, even the greatest heroes are afraid of what they don’t know, and the morning light always brings the truth!

frases.texto: Chapter 15. The Helmet of Mambrino. A Helmet that Shines in the Rain
frases.fala: Chapter 15. The Helmet of Mambrino. A Helmet that Shines in the Rain

frases.texto: As they went on down the road, soft clouds covered the sky and a light RAIN began to fall.
frases.fala: As they went on down the road, soft clouds covered the sky and a light rain began to fall.

frases.texto: Far away, a village BARBER was coming along, nice and calm, on his little donkey.
frases.fala: Far away, a village barber was coming along, nice and calm, on his little donkey.

frases.texto: To keep his new hat dry, he had put a brass basin on his head, and it shone in the rain like a magic mirror!
frases.fala: To keep his new hat dry, he had put a brass basin on his head, and it shone in the rain like a magic mirror!

frases.texto: Don Quixote’s eyes went wide with wonder: “Look, Sancho, the greatest treasure in the world!
frases.fala: Don Quixote’s eyes went wide with wonder: Look, Sancho, the greatest treasure in the world!

frases.texto: That warrior is wearing the famous HELMET OF MAMBRINO, the magic helmet that makes whoever wears it unbeatable!”
frases.fala: That warrior is wearing the famous helmet of mambrino, the magic helmet that makes whoever wears it unbeatable!

frases.texto: With his oak lance pointing forward, the knight charged at a gallop.
frases.fala: With his oak lance pointing forward, the knight charged at a gallop.

frases.texto: “Help!
frases.fala: Help!

frases.texto: Help!” cried the poor barber, terrified of that man in armour.
frases.fala: Help! cried the poor barber, terrified of that man in armour.

frases.texto: He jumped off his donkey and ran away through the wheat, leaving the basin lying on the grass!
frases.fala: He jumped off his donkey and ran away through the wheat, leaving the basin lying on the grass!

frases.texto: Don Quixote put the basin on his head, very grandly: it was too big and a bit wobbly, and it almost covered his eyes, but to him it shone like a king’s purest gold.
frases.fala: Don Quixote put the basin on his head, very grandly: it was too big and a bit wobbly, and it almost covered his eyes, but to him it shone like a king’s purest gold.

frases.texto: Sancho laughed so much that he had to sit down on the grass to get his breath back!
